common_name: Emma Kay Black Walnut (Heavy-Bearing Thin-Shelled Named Black Walnut)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees while dormant in late winter in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, well away from gardens and other juglone-sensitive plants; Emma Kay is grafted onto black walnut rootstock and eventually becomes a large shade tree.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, sited well away from tomatoes, apples, and other plants sensitive to the juglone this species releases into the surrounding soil. Emma Kay is a Midwestern-selected black walnut cultivar valued among home-orchard nut growers for consistently heavy annual crops and an above-average kernel-to-shell ratio, which makes cracking and picking out whole kernel halves noticeably easier than with wild seedling trees. The tree grows vigorously into a large, cold-hardy shade tree, so give it plenty of room away from structures and smaller plantings. Nuts drop in a thick green husk in early fall that should be removed promptly to prevent staining and mold before curing the shells for a few weeks in a dry, well-ventilated spot.
sources: University of Missouri Center for Agroforestry
